selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What change in the sky at nightfall is described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The last light of day disappears, and darkness covers the world.

questions.question: What does this change between day and night remind the reader about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that Allah controls great changes in creation with ease.

questions.question: How is the change from day to night compared to the change from summer to winter?
questions.answer: Both are shown as signs that Allah turns one state into another by His wisdom and power.

questions.question: What does the fading of people’s remaining آثار, or traces, in the world call to mind?
questions.answer: It brings to mind that living things pass away and move on to another world.

questions.question: What bigger event does the passage connect to the destruction of this temporary world?
questions.answer: It connects it to the coming of the hereafter, which is lasting and much greater.

questions.question: How is this worldly life described in comparison to the hereafter?
questions.answer: This world is described as limited, brief, and low, while the hereafter is wide, lasting, and majestic.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone deserves to be loved and worshipped as the true Master?
questions.answer: Only Allah, the One who changes all things and controls every stage of creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage say that only one true object of worship can exist?
questions.answer: Because only the One who can transform night and day, the seasons, and this world into the next has real authority over everything.

questions.question: What moment of the day is the passage mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about the time of ‘Isha, when night has begun.

questions.question: What happens to the edge of the sky at that time?
questions.answer: The remaining brightness disappears from it.

questions.question: What lesson can a believer take from the coming of night?
questions.answer: A believer can learn that Allah is the One who manages the world and changes it however He wills.

questions.question: Besides day and night, what other natural change is mentioned as a similar example?
questions.answer: The passage mentions summer turning into winter.

questions.question: What human reality is suggested by the passing away of people’s remaining works?
questions.answer: It suggests that nothing in this world lasts forever and that people move on after death.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to this present world?
questions.answer: It will come to an end and be replaced by the everlasting world of the hereafter.

questions.question: Which qualities of the hereafter make it different from this world in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as spacious, permanent, and full of greatness.

questions.question: What main idea does the final sentence of the passage teach about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah alone has complete power to create, remove, and replace all things, so He alone deserves worship.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the arrival of night in one simple image?
questions.answer: It describes night as wrapping the universe after the day’s light fades.

questions.question: What does the turning of day into night show about Allah’s dominion?
questions.answer: It shows that His rule is active, powerful, and fully in control.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the sun and moon while talking about ‘Isha time?
questions.answer: To show that even the greatest parts of creation are under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does the passing of time do to the traces left behind in this world?
questions.answer: It gradually wipes them away.

questions.question: What idea about death and the next life is drawn from that erasing?
questions.answer: It points to the truth that this life ends and leads to a different world beyond it.

questions.question: What feelings are created by the description of the world’s final end?
questions.answer: It creates awe, seriousness, and a sense that this world is not meant to last.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast the value of this world with the value of the next world?
questions.answer: It shows this world as temporary and small, but the next world as lasting and noble.

questions.question: What conclusion should a reader make about whom to worship?
questions.answer: The reader should conclude that only Allah deserves worship, since He alone controls every change in creation.
